Quick summary of what I found this round, talking through it like we're all in the same channel:

I dug into the actual gate failure before touching anything, and the `iterate_scope` diagnosis doesn't hold up against the real files. I grepped every `.accessibilityIdentifier` in `Features/` and `Shared/` and all 17 declared flow tokens are already wired, correctly, with matching `.accessibilityLabel`s alongside them: `authGate.signInWithAppleButton`, `podOnboarding.createPodButton/joinPodButton`, `createPod.nameField/confirmButton`, `joinPod.codeField/confirmButton`, `relayBoard.postRequestButton/firstRequestCard`, `requestComposer.noteField/submitButton`, and all five `requestDetail.*` buttons plus `viewReceiptButton`. Nothing's missing. So "identifiers wired for AuthGate but never carried downstream" isn't what's happening.

I traced why the crawler still only sees the sign-in button, and it's structural, not cosmetic: `AppSession.bootstrap()` (Features/App/AppSession.swift:56-65) calls `api.health()` and routes to `.authGate` before it ever checks Keychain for a session — and `PulseRelayApp.swift`'s `backendBaseURL` is still the literal placeholder `https://pulse-relay.invalid` (confirmed — no fly.toml/railway.json/render.yaml/Procfile anywhere in the tree, so nothing's ever been deployed). On top of that, real `SignInWithAppleButton` opens a system-owned sheet no crawler can drive. There's already a partial answer for that second problem — `PulseRelayApp.seedUITestSessionIfRequested` behind `-uiTestSeedSession` — but the UITests file itself says plainly it's not enough alone, and it isn't: even a seeded session never gets past the health-gate with no real backend. This is exactly the same gap `final_review` already called NO-GO on.

So the honest fix isn't in my lane's files. `AppSession.swift` and `PulseRelayApp.swift` are primary_ui/integrator-owned, and the actual unblock is either a real deployed backend (the fleet's own #1 follow-up priority already) or a deliberate, explicitly-authorized crawl-mode bypass — not something I should quietly bolt on from the polish_resilience lane.

While I was in there I also verified my own lane's actual territory rather than inventing busywork: `AsyncActionButton`, `DestructiveActionConfirmation` (correctly wired to release/withdraw via `confirmDestructiveAction`, my earlier grep for the type name was just a miss), `BeaconCard`/`BeaconMotionState` (0.9s pulse, 0.45s identical winner/loser spring, 0.15s Reduce Motion crossfade, identical haptic — matches DEC-design_handoff-004 exactly), `StateViews`, `SyncBannerState`, `ElapsedTimeFormatting`, and `SettingsRow` are all already correctly built and consistent with the locked decisions. No design-lint violations (`DS.IconSize.*` tokens only, no raw literals). And confirmed my three "claimed" backlog tasks (T-002/T-004/T-006 — request state machine, account soft-delete, pod timezone) are already fully satisfied in `backend/server/models/{request,account,pod}.ts` from an earlier wave — stale carryover, nothing to redo.

**Files changed this round: none.** Everything genuinely in my lane's scope was already correct; making speculative edits to already-working shared components would just add risk, not reduce it.

**What remains, for whoever picks this up next:** the UI-crawl gate cannot pass until either the backend gets a real deployed host (swap `PulseRelayApp.backendBaseURL`) or someone explicitly authorizes a crawl-mode override to `AppSession.bootstrap()`'s health-gate — that decision belongs to the integrator, not a silent lane edit.

**To verify:** `grep -rn "accessibilityIdentifier" ios/PulseRelay/App/Features ios/PulseRelay/App/Shared` shows all 17 tokens present; `cat ios/PulseRelay/App/PulseRelayApp.swift` shows the `.invalid` placeholder host still in place.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
